core.title: Make every interlocking structural residual explicit, narrow, and bound to an acceptance and validator
core.given: An interlocking subject (standalone or embedded in another planning artifact) that has one or more structural residuals, whether declared or relied on without being written down.
core.when: The planner authors or edits the interlocking, or the interlocking is validated at the CONFIRM phase.
core.then: Make each structural residual explicit and narrow, and bind it to both an acceptance reference and a validator reference.
prefer: Write each residual down as a declared residual with its own identifier, stating the one structural gap it covers.
Bind each residual to a concrete acceptance reference and validator reference that resolve to an existing acceptance and validator.
avoid: Leaving a structural residual implicit: relying on it without writing it down as a residual.
Broad residuals that cover several unrelated gaps.
Missing, placeholder, or dangling acceptance or validator references added just to satisfy the presence check.
core.why: A structural residual is the escape hatch from surfacing something directly; it stays safe only if it is explicit, narrow, and still covered by an acceptance and a validator.
evidence: The check that validates interlocking structural residuals passes at the CONFIRM phase.
Each residual of the interlocking has an identifier, an acceptance reference and a validator reference; on failure, the check reports the interlocking, the residual, both references, and the reason.
verification: Conditional presence check over the interlocking subject: it applies only when a structural residual is present in the interlocking; it then requires that the residual is explicit and narrow and has both an acceptance reference and a validator reference.

Runs at phase CONFIRM with confirm-blocking enforcement; the subject is the interlocking, tracked at subject level and not tied to any file kind; it applies to all residuals of the interlocking, changed or not.
On failure, report the interlocking, the residual, its acceptance reference, its validator reference, and the reason.

What the check does not cover: the mechanical scan reads only declared residuals. Residuals relied on but not written down, and interlockings embedded in other planning artifacts, cannot be read from a declaration list (an empty residual declaration alone does not establish absence of residuals) and remain judgment-dependent.
Validator, validation template/variant, and finding ids of this rule are realization details; each stack names its own check for the same obligation.

values: an interlocking subject is authored, edited, or validated and has a structural residual (declared, or relied on but not declared)
a finding of this rule's check failing: a structural residual of an interlocking is not explicit, not narrow, or not bound to an acceptance and a validator

fires: CONFIRM validates an interlocking subject (standalone or embedded in another planning artifact) that has structural residuals, including residuals not changed in this work.
A planner authors or edits an interlocking that relies on a structural residual which is not written down as a residual.
A structural residual in an interlocking lacks an acceptance reference or a validator reference.
A structural residual is vague or broad rather than narrow.
doesNotFire: An interlocking that has no structural residual at all, neither declared nor relied on implicitly (an empty residual declaration alone does not establish this).
Planning artifacts that contain no interlocking subject.

bunOnly.reason: Names this stack's concrete validator (a sequence-diagram sanity test); validator ids of a single rule are realization details, so the core names the check generically.
The finding id names the ATDD-Bun validator; other stacks report this rule's failure under their own finding id.

bunOnly.reason: The validation taxonomy and the variant id belong to the ATDD-Bun checker; the core states the same conditional-presence obligation without the checker's ids.

neutralityNotes: This convention is a planning-method rule over plan-artifact content. Its vocabulary (interlocking, structural residual, acceptance reference, validator reference, the planner role, the CONFIRM phase) is method-level rather than stack-level, so the core keeps it and names no stack, runtime, path, or file kind. The concrete field spellings residual_id / acceptance_ref / validator_ref / interlocking_id are generalized to identifier/reference phrasing; bun.json remains the worked reference example with the exact schema. The only realization-specific content is the validator test id, the validation template/variant ids, and the finding id (bunOnly); the core's verification describes the conditional-presence check generically, including its limitation that a declaration scan sees only declared residuals while implicit residuals and embedded interlockings stay judgment-dependent, exactly as in bun.json. Because activation is subject-level with no file classification assumed, the core needs no paths, suffixes, URN shapes, or idiom constructs from the profile; profileRequirements and proposedKeys are therefore empty. Severity 3 and disposition strict are kept in core verification, not the profile.
